{"self_assessment": "Impact: I drew the fish outline on the pad and laid the top edge from the nose, so everyone had a clear picture to trace from. I can't confirm the judge recognised the fish, since I didn't see the push result. Going by the last inspections, the body and fin were connected back to start, and the open joins were at the arms, which we were still working on at the end.

Execution: The top edge went down cleanly. I also caught that the tail was being laid from the wrong end, but I flagged it late, so Tom had to redo the whole tail near the deadline. I kept my hands off stroke 2 as agreed. My weakness was verbosity: I repeated status updates a lot, which probably slowed the table, and I didn't check the lower arm join myself early enough.

Collaboration: Tom, Maya and Leo all took clear pieces, and Leo's inspection helped us find where things stood. There were some crossed messages, such as when Maya asked me what Tom had said and I answered second-hand. I should have pulled Tom and Maya into a direct check instead.

Leadership: I set the plan, the nose-to-tail rule and the join checks. But I should have checked the tail's direction before Tom laid it, not after. I also didn't settle who owned the lower arm until late, so Leo and Maya ended up doubling up near the join. Next time I'd confirm direction and assign one owner per join before the first domino goes down, and keep my updates shorter."}
